ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, managers, and UBOs against Egyptian Ministry of Interior blacklists, the Central Bank of Egypt sanctions lists, UN Security Council consolidated lists, and OFAC SDN List. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) are subject to enhanced due diligence under Law No. 80 of 2002, including source of wealth documentation, beneficial-ownership chain verification, and senior-management sign-off before any share acquisition or transaction.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) Company Registration E-Service Portal (www.gafi.gov.eg)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name of an Egyptian LLC must be in Arabic script and unique within the commercial registry. A Latin transliteration may be registered as a secondary name but does not constitute the official legal name. The name must be descriptive or arbitrary but not misleading, cannot indicate an unlicensed regulated activity, cannot contain foreign political or religious connotations, and must avoid any direct reference to the Republic itself unless expressly authorized.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservations are not extendable; upon expiry, a fresh reservation application must be submitted. After a name rejection, the incorporation agent may file a written administrative appeal with the GAFI Complaints Committee within 30 calendar days of the rejection notice, setting out grounds of distinctiveness and any trademark registration. The appellant may simultaneously apply for a corrected name. If the appeal is refused, the applicant may challenge the decision before the Economic Court in Cairo under Egyptian administrative judicial review procedure within 60 days of the denial.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office is not permitted for initial GAFI incorporation; the LLC must have a physical registered address in Egypt supported by a duly executed lease agreement or notarized deeds of ownership. For a mobile software utility company, a serviced office or co-working suite with dedicated meeting space and letterhead can qualify if it is the actual seat of management, but a rented mailbox-only address cannot.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate; unannounced verification visits by GAFI inspectors and police are possible within the first 24 months of incorporation. Estimated annual inspection probability for a registered office of a low-risk software LLC is approximately 10–20%.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018), Articles 26-47 and 51-54; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, Chapters III and VI
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), Companies Registration Department, Commercial Registry, Ministry of Investment
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation and Commercial Registry Certificate, based on notarized Arabic Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to LLCs under Law 159/1981, as amended; founders may declare capital in EGP or foreign currency. Escrow/bank deposit rules are not triggered for a standard LLC unless the approved activity is financial, insurance, or otherwise subject to sector-specific capital regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: By written resolution of the sole founding member of the LLC under Law No. 159/1981: 1. Formation: the LLC is established with the attached Memorandum and Articles of Association. 2. Subscription: all nominal capital shares are subscribed and the required consideration has been paid or is recorded as receivable in accordance with the capital declaration. 3. Office: the registered office is adopted at [address], Cairo, which shall be the legal seat for statutory and service purposes. 4. Officers: [Name] is appointed CEO and [Name] Compliance Officer, each authorized to file incorporation documents, open bank accounts, and represent the Company before GAFI and tax authorities. 5. Effect: all customary proceedings and documents of incorporation are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Shareek / Invest in Egypt online portal, Companies Registration Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the GAFI electronic incorporation portal, select LLC formation, submit the proposed Arabic and English trade names, and verify uniqueness against the GAFI name index. The reservation is auto-generated after compliance with Arabic naming rules and country constraints and is valid for two months.
required_dossiers: Written incorporation authority or authorized attorney mandate
Valid national ID or passport of each founding partner
Passport copy translated and notarized if non-Egyptian partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit a new name request on the same portal with an amended listing; alternatively, file a written objection to the GAFI Name Registration Committee for formal reconsideration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Arabic Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Notary Authority (Ministry of Justice) and GAFI legal verification desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Arabic Articles of Association, have all founding partners execute the document physically or electronically, and obtain notarization from the Notary Authority. Upload the notarized Articles to the GAFI portal for statutory review, ensuring inclusion of capital structure, registered office, manager powers, and transfer restrictions.
required_dossiers: Residence certificates or passports of partners
Notarized power of attorney if an agent executes
Capital declaration statement signed by partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where GAFI returns review comments, execute a supplementary notarial correction deed and resubmit within 15 working days. If the Notary Authority queries a foreign-language document, submit a certified legal translation and re-notarize the translation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registry registration and certificate of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry under GAFI, Ministry of Investment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Articles of Association together with the incorporation application form and supporting dossiers at the Commercial Registry. The Registry verifies compliance, assigns the legal form and company number, records the registered office and managers, and issues the Certificate of Incorporation and the Commercial Registration extract.
required_dossiers: Registered office lease contract or owner's consent
Valid ID or passport of managers and partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries a deficiency, cure the defect within 10 working days by submitting corrected certificates, lease replacement, or compliant amendments. A rejection may be appealed administratively to GAFI's First Instance Committee within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration with the Egyptian Tax Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), headquarters or district tax office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Tax Registration Form (Form 1) through the ETA online portal or local branch after obtaining the Commercial Registry certificate. Submit statutory documents to obtain the Tax Identification Number (TIN), VAT certificate if voluntary or mandatory under Law 67/2016, and employee payroll/tax withholding regime. The company must file zero returns until actual economic activity commences.
required_dossiers: National ID or passport of partners and managers
Bank account certificate if any capital is deposited
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ETA denies or delays registration, request a written refusal, submit an administrative complaint under Tax Law 67/2016, and follow up with the ETA electronic tracker. If the denial is based on incorrect business classification, file a correction and appeal with the relevant ETA committee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Employer registration with the National Organization for Social Insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Government of Egypt National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI), local insurance office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the LLC as an employer and enroll managing officers or employees under the Insurance Law No. 79 of 1975, as amended, by filing Form 1 and Form 2 at the appropriate NOSI office. Contribution rates and insurable minimum salaries are applied per the latest annual ministerial decree of the Ministry of Finance.
required_dossiers: Officer appointment minutes or resolution copy
Passport or national ID of insured officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If NOSI assesses excessive contributions, submit a corrected salary declaration and request relief through NOSI's appeals procedure; unpaid back contributions may be re-calculated and paid in installments upon request.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: General Authority for Industrial Development (GAID) — not applicable; no industrial or manufacturing facility is licensed for ISIC 6201 mobile software services
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required for pure digital application development and distribution; distribution is effected via Apple App Store IAP and Google Play Billing without Egyptian operational permit

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office-based software development activity without point-source emissions, land alteration, or wastewater discharge
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable; administrative office waste is handled under municipal solid waste regulations (Law No. 202 of 2020); no VOC, industrial wastewater, or combustion thresholds apply to software-only operations

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For the registered office: obtain a civil defense fire safety certificate from the competent Civil Defense Department prior to operational use of premises. Occupational workplace clearance is required under Labour Law No. 12 of 2003, including emergency exit inspection, fire extinguisher readiness, and first-aid facilities; structural load inspection is only required for heavy equipment, which is not applicable to software development.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance, through the ETA Taxpayer Portal and applicable integrated tax-registration services at https://www.eta.gov.eg. The ETA administers income tax, value-added tax, tax registration, electronic invoicing, and electronic receipt compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: An Egyptian limited liability company must obtain an ETA tax registration certificate and tax identification number after incorporation and commercial registration. The standard process is: (1) complete incorporation and obtain the commercial registration and constitutional documents from the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones or the competent incorporation authority; (2) obtain or document the registered office, lease, utility evidence, and authorized-manager details; (3) submit the tax-registration application electronically through the ETA Taxpayer Portal or through the competent ETA office, as applicable; (4) provide the commercial registration, articles of association, national identification or passport details of the authorized representative, power of attorney, registered-address evidence, and banking or business information requested by the ETA; (5) undergo address or document verification where required; (6) receive the tax registration certificate and tax identification number; and (7) separately register for VAT if the company conducts taxable activities and reaches the statutory threshold, or if compulsory registration applies to a category not subject to the general threshold. A foreign company carrying on taxable business in Egypt generally requires an Egyptian tax registration number and, where applicable, a VAT registration number. A nonresident digital-service supplier making supplies to Egyptian consumers may be required to use the ETA nonresident or simplified VAT registration process and comply with collection, filing, and payment rules applicable to nonresident suppliers. The ETA may require certified Arabic translations, legalization or apostille of foreign corporate documents, an Egyptian tax representative, and evidence of the Egyptian taxable activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt has no general United States-style check-the-box election for an Egyptian limited liability company. An Egyptian LLC is ordinarily treated as a separate corporate taxpayer and is subject to Egyptian corporate income tax on its taxable income. A nonresident company is generally taxed on Egyptian-source income or income attributable to an Egyptian permanent establishment. Tax treatment may be affected by a valid double taxation agreement, permanent-establishment analysis, free-zone or special economic-zone legislation, investment incentives, or a statutory exemption, but these are not entity-classification elections. Egyptian tax law does not provide a general hybrid-mismatch election that allows an LLC to elect transparent or pass-through treatment for Egyptian tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value Added Tax Law No. 67 of 2016 and its executive regulations
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 of annual taxable turnover is the general VAT registration threshold under the VAT regime. Registration may also be compulsory without reliance on the threshold for specified goods, services, importers, exporters, and other statutory categories. A company supplying taxable mobile software, subscriptions, in-app functionality, or related digital services in Egypt must assess both the threshold and any sector-specific or nonresident digital-service registration rules. Imports are generally subject to import VAT at the applicable rate, unless a statutory exemption or special treatment applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Egypt operates an ETA electronic invoicing system for business-to-business and other covered transactions, using the ETA platform, approved integration methods, electronic signatures, and structured invoice data. Covered taxpayers must obtain ETA credentials, register or onboard the relevant taxpayer and devices or systems where required, issue compliant electronic invoices, transmit invoice data to the ETA, and retain electronic records. ETA electronic invoice procedures generally involve digital signing, unique invoice identifiers, validation, and QR-code or equivalent verification features. Electronic receipt requirements apply to covered business-to-consumer transactions through the ETA electronic receipt system, including the use of approved point-of-sale, application, or system integration arrangements. The exact implementation date and scope depend on the taxpayer category, transaction type, and ETA implementation notices. An app-store freemium model must distinguish supplies made by the Egyptian LLC from supplies made by Apple or Google as merchant of record. Platform statements, commission invoices, customer location evidence, VAT treatment, and ETA reporting must reconcile with the entity's contractual role. Failure to issue or transmit a required electronic invoice or receipt can result in administrative penalties, invoice disallowance, tax assessments, and other enforcement measures under Egyptian tax law.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Egyptian VAT may apply at zero percent to qualifying exports of goods and qualifying services supplied to customers outside Egypt, subject to the statutory conditions and implementing rules. For goods, the goods must be exported from Egypt and supported by customs evidence showing actual export. For services, the service must generally be supplied to a nonresident recipient and used or enjoyed outside Egypt; services performed in or relating to Egyptian real estate, goods, events, or activities in Egypt may fail the offshore-service conditions. An app or digital service is not automatically zero-rated merely because the customer pays through Apple or Google or because the platform is located outside Egypt. The company must establish the supplier of record, customer residence, place of use or enjoyment, contractual scope, transaction value, and payment trail. Export VAT refunds or input-tax credits require valid VAT registration, compliant tax invoices, evidence that input VAT relates to taxable or zero-rated activity, and reconciliation to VAT returns. VAT input relating to exempt activities is generally not recoverable.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration or equivalent Egyptian customs export record showing clearance and actual export of the goods
Commercial invoice, packing list, transport document, and Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or other carrier evidence, where goods are exported
Foreign customer contract, purchase order, or service agreement identifying the nonresident recipient and the exported goods or offshore service
Evidence of delivery, foreign use or enjoyment, and customer location for exported services or digital services
Inward Remittance Certificate, bank credit advice, or other acceptable banking evidence linking foreign-currency proceeds to the exported transaction, subject to applicable banking rules
ETA-compliant tax invoices, credit notes, electronic invoices or receipts, and VAT-return reconciliation
Foreign exchange and payment-platform settlement statements, including Apple or Google merchant statements where a platform is contractually involved
Corporate accounting records, export sales ledger, customs reconciliation, and supporting documentation for recoverable input VAT
Import VAT and input-tax documentation for costs claimed in a VAT refund or credit application
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The 180-day period should be treated as a compliance-control assumption for collection or repatriation of export proceeds where applicable under current Egyptian foreign-exchange, banking, customs, or sectoral rules; the company must confirm the operative requirement with its Egyptian bank and current Central Bank and customs guidance because the deadline and exceptions can vary by transaction and exporter status. The ETA may deny zero-rating, recover improperly refunded or credited input VAT, assess output VAT at the applicable rate, impose late-payment interest and statutory penalties, and disallow unsupported expenses or invoices where export conditions are not proven. False customs declarations, fabricated invoices, concealed domestic use, circular payments, sham offshore customers, or fraudulent refund claims may expose the company and responsible officers to tax, customs, accounting, and criminal liability. Consequences can include retrospective VAT assessments, clawback of refunds and credits, interest, administrative fines, suspension or cancellation of tax registration or electronic-invoicing access, customs penalties, denial of future refund claims, and prosecution under applicable tax, customs, anti-money-laundering, and penal laws. Documentation should be retained for the statutory tax-record retention period and made available in Arabic or with an acceptable certified translation when requested by the ETA or another competent authority.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt maintains current-account convertibility for legitimate trade and service transactions through the CBE interbank market. Capital-account inflows and outflows are substantially regulated by CBE foreign-exchange instructions under Law No. 88 of 2003 and Investment Law No. 72 of 2017. Non-resident profit remittances are permitted after corporate income tax and applicable withholding tax are settled, provided that: the Egyptian LLC has filed audited financial statements; a tax clearance certificate has been obtained; the funds to be remitted are held in the LLC’s licensed Egyptian bank account; and the remittance is supported by a board resolution and dividend distribution minutes. Practical friction may arise during periods of FX shortage because CBE and commercial banks prioritise essential imports, fuel, medicines, and strategic commodities; therefore, app-store revenue held offshore should be routed to Egypt through transparent SWIFT channels and declared for balance-of-payments reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under current CBE policy, export proceeds must be repatriated through, and received by, an Egyptian licensed bank rather than paid directly to an unlicensed offshore account. For merchandise exports, the customary statutory expectation is that the full invoice value must be received by the Egyptian bank within 60 to 90 days from the date of shipment, subject to the underlying commercial terms and CBE-approved exceptions. There is no blanket mandatory conversion percentage; after the 2016 FX liberalisation, exporters may retain export proceeds in foreign-currency accounts with licensed Egyptian banks. However, 100% of export-related collection must enter the Egyptian banking system, be declared to the CBE, and be capable of being matched against the underlying customs or service-export documentation. For digital services and mobile application proceeds sourced from Apple App Store Connect and Google Play Billing, the revenue constitutes services exports and must be received in a bank-supervised FX account, supported by monthly platform statements, tax invoices, and payment-provider reconciliation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for use as a principal corporate treasury account. Offshore digital EMI firms are not licensed by the CBE and may not lawfully maintain Egyptian-pound settlement accounts, collect consumer payments on behalf of Egyptian businesses, or hold Egyptian banking licences. Such entities cannot provide compliant EGP clearing rails and are not accepted as replacement accounts for mandatory CBE-monitored trade or capital flows. They may be used only for peripheral pre-collection of USD/EUR from offshore app stores before the funds are formally routed into the Egyptian banking system, provided full beneficiary and source-of-funds trail is retained. Reliance on an offshore EMI to avoid CBE controls is an AML/CTF red flag and will generally result in bank rejection or account freezing in Egypt.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For an Egyptian LLC with non-resident shareholders, at least the legal representative or a formally appointed authorised signatory must usually appear in person at the branch in Egypt to complete the corporate KYC interview. Some Egyptian banks now permit a hybrid remote pre-verification step for Egyptian-resident directors using the CBE-backed digital onboarding infrastructure, but non-resident directors and ultimate beneficial owners should expect physical attendance, a board-endorsed resolution, original corporate documents certified by the General Authority for Investment (GAFI), commercial registry extracts, tax card, and notarised/legalised passport copies. If no director can travel, a notarised power of attorney apostilled by the foreign jurisdiction and accepted by the Egyptian bank is mandatory; the attorney must appear physically and must not be a sanctioned or negative-news person. Physical verification of the business premise or a virtual-office explanation is also required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership structure with offshore shareholders and no clear source of wealth
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: GAFI certificate; commercial registry extract; LLC constitutional documents; notarised and legalised shareholder register; board resolution confirming equity contribution; passport copies of all UBOs; CVs and professional references; source-of-wealth statements; bank reference letters from the shareholders’ banks; signed declaration of tax residence and anti-money-laundering compliance policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue derived from decentralised app-store sales with no conventional invoiced customer relationships
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apple App Store Connect payout reports; Google Play Console monthly revenue statements; payment-provider settlement records; store tax withholding certificates and tax invoices; end-user licence agreement and privacy policy; a transaction-level reconciliation log proving app purchases are attributable to the Egyptian LLC’s registered developer account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency, low-value inbound digital receipts creating an ML-typology concern
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written AML/CTF policy; enterprise risk assessment; customer risk-rating methodology; transaction-monitoring system overview; designation of an Egyptian AML compliance officer; staff training records; suspicious-transaction reporting protocol; audit trail linking each payout cycle to the app's published revenue dashboard.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Low minimum capital and absence of physical inventory or manufacturing assets
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Leased office or virtual-office agreement with utility bill; company website and active app store listings; payroll records and Egyptian social insurance declarations; software development contracts; technical support routes; GAFI investment certificate; board minutes proving actual digital product operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payment processors or app stores remitting in foreign currency on behalf of unknown end customers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Collection-agent agreements with Apple and Google; fully executed developer-program contracts; monthly settlement certifications; beneficial-ownership declaration for payment processor accounts; legal memorandum describing the collection and settlement flow; bank confirmation that funds originate from compliant card networks.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders must subscribe to the LLC’s equity through a formal capital-contribution instruction and transfer capital via SWIFT MT103 from their own bank accounts. The receiving Egyptian bank requires the remittance to include a CBE balance-of-payments purpose code corresponding to inward direct investment/equity capital, together with the GAFI registration number and the LLC’s commercial registration number. Supporting documents must include the board/shareholder resolution approving the capital increase or initial subscription, share-allocation table, amended articles of association, source-of-funds evidence, and a signed declaration for CBE foreign-direct-investment reporting. Cash deposits, crypto transfers, personal accounts, or funds routed through a non-related third party will not be accepted. The bank will issue an inward remittance advice and will register the transaction with the CBE’s foreign-direct-investment and balance-of-payments database.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments for software licences, cloud infrastructure, legal fees, marketing services, and app-store infrastructure support should be cleared using SWIFT MT103 from the LLC’s Egyptian bank account, supported by the underlying commercial contract, invoice, tax invoice, and the CBE outbound transfer application. Physical-goods payments, if any, should be made through an irrevocable documentary commercial letter of credit advised and settled through the correspondent banking network, with the Egyptian bank checking the import documentation against the CBE’s import prioritisation and importer-registration rules. All outbound transfers must be from the LLC’s licensed Egyptian account and must disclose the precise CBE remittance purpose code; failure to provide a valid tax card, transfer-pricing documentation for related-party royalties or services, and audited financial basis for profit distribution may cause rejection. Banks may also require a signed undertaking that the underlying transaction is genuine and free of sanctions exposure.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla OTC USD/EGP forward contracts with a CBE-licensed bank, limited to the LLC’s documented receivables or payables exposure.
USD/EGP FX swap contracts for temporary conversion and reconversion of operational liquidity.
Cross-currency interest rate swap between USD floating-rate and EGP fixed-rate obligations where there is an interest-bearing balance-sheet exposure.
Plain-vanilla USD/EGP options purchased for hedging purposes only, requiring a written underlying-exposure statement and board approval.

Offshore non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts may be used only as a fallback hedging tool for EGP exposure that cannot otherwise be delivered onshore, provided the bank is satisfied that the hedge is genuine and not speculative; speculative NDF-only structures are not permitted.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registry Renewal (Commercial Extract / Good Standing Plaque)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI – Commercial Registry Section (Ministry of Trade and Industry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each anniversary of the company’s commercial registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal yields administrative late fines beginning at EGP 100 per day (capped at EGP 5,000); failure to renew for 12 months triggers suspension of the entity’s commercial record and potential strike-off by GAFI.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the end of the fiscal year (fiscal year is 31 December; due by 31 March)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Untimely filing exposes the company to a fine of EGP 500 plus EGP 50 per day of delay; persistent non-filing for two consecutive years can lead to a temporary freeze of certificates and legal strike-off initiated by GAFI.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the anniversary of incorporation; also within 15 days of any shareholding transfer or ownership change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file is subject to administrative fines and personal criminal liability for managers; under Companies Law 72/2017 penalties include imprisonment up to one year and/or a fine of EGP 5,000–200,000. Continued noncompliance triggers suspension of shareholder rights and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Local Municipality Commercial License Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Before 31 January of each calendar year for continuing operations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-renewal results in temporary closure of premises, a fine of EGP 1,000–10,000, and referral to commercial registry to mark non-operation, which may trigger dissolution for inactivity.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All LLCs must appoint at least one statutory auditor. A compulsory independent audit is statutorily required when paid-up capital exceeds EGP 5,000,000, annual revenue exceeds EGP 10,000,000, or total assets exceed EGP 7,000,000. Below those thresholds, members may unanimously waive the audit but must still prepare financial statements in conformity with EAS.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) as mandated by Companies Law 72/2017 and implementing ministerial decrees; EAS are substantially aligned with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Within 30 days of the incorporation anniversary, the LLC must file an electronic UBO confirmation via the GAFI UBO portal, verifying all current beneficial owners and declaring any shareholding transfers that occurred during the preceding year. Any share transfer during the year must be accompanied by a revised UBO schedule within 15 days of the transfer. A beneficial owner is any natural person directly or indirectly holding more than 25% of equity or voting rights, or otherwise exercising control through other means.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partner Meetings / Minutes (Minute Book)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No automatic statutory tax holiday applies to a standard Egyptian LLC under Law No. 91/2005. A 50% CIT reduction may be granted on a discretionary Cabinet basis under Article 59 for projects of strategic economic importance; entities located inside the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone) may elect a 0% CIT regime for up to 5 years under Law No. 83/2002. A standard app-development LLC outside a free zone is subject to the flat 22.5% rate on worldwide income as an Egyptian tax resident.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 22 (Annual Corporate Income Tax Return) filed electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-filing portal at taxa.gov.eg
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 4 months from the fiscal year-end (e.g. by 30 April for a 31 December year-end). The final balance of CIT is due at the filing deadline; advance installments based on the previous year's tax are payable during the year, and a separate annual transfer pricing disclosure form must accompany the return where controlled transactions exceed the statutory threshold.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, commercial registration number, tax card number, registered address, and list of all shareholders/partners with their tax identification numbers
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must be identified with full legal names, country of residence, foreign TIN, and ownership percentage; failure to disclose triggers nondisclosure penalties

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the fiscal year covered by the return
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Egyptian LLC adopts a foreign parent's non-calendar fiscal year, a prior ETA approval must be evidenced; otherwise the calendar year is deemed compulsory

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from mobile application development, in-app sales, subscriptions, advertising, and technical support services
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross billings net of Apple App Store and Google Play platform commissions and applicable VAT; commissions are deductible when supported by proper foreign invoices; revenue derived from Egyptian customers is taxable Egyptian-source income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales, employee remuneration, marketing, cloud hosting, royalties, depreciation, and financing charges, reconciled to the audited financial statements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-deductible items such as unpaid intercompany service fees, excessive royalty rates, and entertainment expenses; cross-border service fees require documentary evidence of actual provision and arm's length pricing

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjusted taxable income after statutory add-backs, exempt income, capital gains computation, and utilization of tax losses carried forward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carry-forwards are strictly limited to 5 years and are forfeited if the majority shareholding changes; intercompany losses are disallowed under the transfer pricing rules

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT due at 22.5%, less advance installments, foreign tax credits, and final net tax payable or refund claim
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits must be supported by foreign tax assessments and are capped at the Egyptian tax attributable to the same foreign income; dividends distributed after filing must be reported to the WHT administration separately

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form No. 22 triggers a monthly delay surcharge of 2% of the tax due for each month or part of a month, plus a fixed fine under the Tax Procedures Law (typically EGP 20,000 to 50,000) for failure to file; continued non-compliance enables the ETA to conduct a deemed assessment, enforce asset attachment, and apply a travel ban against signatory directors.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% (final withholding tax levied on dividends and profit distributions made by an Egyptian LLC to non-resident shareholders and to resident natural persons; resident corporate shareholders may be exempt under domestic participation relief)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced dividend rate under one of Egypt's 50+ double tax agreements, the non-resident recipient must file a treaty relief application with the ETA via the electronic portal before remittance, attaching: (i) an original Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the residence-state tax authority and legalized/apostilled; (ii) a statement of beneficial ownership confirming the recipient is the ultimate beneficiary of the distribution; and (iii) documentary evidence of shareholding percentage and holding period. The Egyptian LLC must retain the ETA's written approval; otherwise 10% WHT is withheld at source and remitted to the ETA within the statutory declaration period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for industrial, commercial, or copyright property used in Egypt: 20% statutory WHT, commonly reduced to 10%–15% under tax treaties; interest on loans and debentures from non-residents: 20% statutory WHT, treaty-reduced typically to 10%–15%; technical service and management fees paid to non-residents without a permanent establishment: 20% statutory WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The Egyptian Transfer Pricing Guidelines (ETA, 2020) mandate a Local File where aggregate controlled transactions with related parties equal or exceed EGP 8 million in a fiscal year; a Master File is mandatory at or above EGP 30 million in aggregate controlled transactions; Country-by-Country Reporting applies to multinational groups whose consolidated group revenue equals or exceeds EGP 22.5 billion (approximately EUR 750 million). Documentation must be submitted in Arabic or English within 30 days of an ETA request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not operate a standalone UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime, but the ETA applies a statutory General Anti-Avoidance Rule under Law 91/2005 (Articles 36 and 39) authorizing recharacterization of artificial transactions lacking commercial substance. Treaty relief and TP deductibility are denied to shell vehicles without local employees, office premises, genuine decision-making, and risk-bearing capacity; an Egyptian LLC acting solely as a pass-through for mobile-app IP profits is exposed to full CIT reassessment, penalty surcharges, and loss of DTA protection.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of App Store and Google Play revenue, falsification of accounting records, use of offshore nominee accounts to hide Egyptian-source income, or fictitious intercompany invoicing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment of not less than 2 years and not exceeding 5 years and a fine of three to five times the amount of tax evaded under Law 91/2005 as amended; conviction is published at the taxpayer's expense and the company's tax card may be suspended
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, general managers, and authorized signatories who directed or participated in the concealment are personally subject to criminal conviction, travel bans, seizure of personal assets, and civil restitution of the evaded tax on a joint and several basis

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold and Remit WHT
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends to a non-resident shareholder, or paying cross-border royalties, interest, or service fees, without withholding the applicable 10%–20% statutory WHT and without obtaining treaty clearance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The under-collected WHT is assessed against the Egyptian LLC as agent, plus the 2% monthly delay surcharge on the unpaid amount and fixed administrative fines under the Tax Procedures Law
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members and financial officers are jointly and severally liable with the company for WHT that was collected but not remitted; aggravated non-remittance is characterized as embezzlement of public funds and triggers imprisonment and asset freezing

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a letterbox Egyptian LLC with no real staff, no physical office, and no operational substance, used solely to route mobile-app royalties or profits through Egyptian treaty provisions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA disregards the entity and reattributes profits to the controlling foreign enterprise, assessing 22.5% CIT on the full reattributed base, adding the 2% monthly delay surcharge, and extending the look-back period to the full 5-year statute of limitations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors face piercing of the corporate veil under the Egyptian Companies Law; courts may order personal reimbursement of reassessed taxes and impose a travel ban and precautionary attachment pending final judgment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing App Store proceeds through unlicensed digital wallets, cryptocurrency exchanges, or informal hawala networks, or maintaining unexplained treasury accounts inconsistent with the declared freemium revenue model
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering and related financing offenses under Law No. 80/2002 (as amended by Law No. 177/2020) carry imprisonment and fines of up to EGP 5 million, confiscation of the laundered funds and related assets, and cancellation of the commercial registration of the operating entity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors involved in layering or concealing transaction proceeds face separate criminal prosecution, permanent disqualification from corporate board service, placement on the Egyptian AML blacklist, and civil liability for the full value of the laundered assets with no cap
